title: DEAD CLIC: debit and credit
lines: | Debit increases (DEAD) | Credit increases (CLIC)
| Drawings | Liabilities
| Expenses and losses | Income and gains
| Assets | Capital
- D-E-A-D: Debit for Drawings, Expenses, Assets.
- C-L-I-C: Credit for Liabilities, Income, Capital.
- A decrease goes on the opposite side.
! Drawings are a debit but not an expense: they never enter profit and loss.

title: Golden rules
lines: | Account type | Rule
| Personal (people, firms, banks) | Debit the receiver, credit the giver
| Real (assets) | Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
| Nominal (expenses, incomes) | Debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains
> Cash sale: Cash comes in (real, Dr); Sales is income (nominal, Cr).
! Outstanding Salaries is a representative personal account; Salaries itself is nominal.

title: Accounting equation
lines: - Assets = Capital + Liabilities
- Capital = Assets − Liabilities
- Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit + New capital − Drawings
- Profit = Closing capital − Opening capital + Drawings − New capital
! Paying a creditor lowers assets and liabilities; capital does not change. Paying an expense lowers assets and capital.

title: Concepts in one line
lines: | Concept | Key idea
| Business entity | Owner and business are separate
| Going concern | Business will continue
| Money measurement | Only money items recorded
| Historical cost | Assets at cost
| Realisation | Sale when goods delivered
| Matching | Expense in the year it helps earn revenue
| Consistency | Same method each year
| Prudence | Provide for losses, not gains
| Materiality | Ignore trivial items' strict treatment

title: Source documents
lines: | Document | Sent by | Shows
| Invoice | Seller | Credit sale
| Debit note | Buyer | Goods returned to seller
| Credit note | Seller | Buyer owes less
| Receipt | Receiver of cash | Cash received
| Cheque counterfoil | Payer | Cheque payment
| Pay-in slip | Depositor | Money paid into bank

title: Subsidiary books
lines: | Book | Records
| Purchases book | Credit purchases of goods for resale
| Sales book | Credit sales of goods
| Purchases returns book | Returns outwards (debit notes)
| Sales returns book | Returns inwards (credit notes)
| Cash book | All cash and bank items
| Journal proper | Fixed assets on credit, opening, adjusting and correcting entries
! Persons are posted one by one; the book total goes to the nominal account.

title: Discounts
lines: - Trade discount: off the list price, never entered in the ledger.
- Cash discount: for prompt payment, always recorded.
- Discount allowed (to customers): a loss, debit, profit and loss.
- Discount received (from suppliers): a gain, credit, profit and loss.
> List Rs 80,000, trade 20 %, cash 5 %: 64,000 − 3,200 = Rs 60,800 received.
! Apply discounts one after another; never add the rates.

title: Trial balance sides
lines: | Debit column | Credit column
| Assets, cash, bank | Capital
| Expenses, purchases | Liabilities, creditors, loans
| Drawings | Sales
| Returns inwards | Returns outwards
| Discount allowed | Discount received
| Opening stock | Bank overdraft
! Closing stock is usually a note below the trial balance, not a balance in it.

title: Errors the trial balance misses
lines: Remember OCPOC:
- O: Omission (transaction left out)
- C: Commission (wrong account, same class)
- P: Principle (capital and revenue confused)
- O: Original entry (wrong amount in the prime book)
- C: Compensating (two errors cancel)
! One-sided errors, wrong sides and casting errors do make it disagree; their difference goes to suspense.

title: Final accounts formulas
lines: - Net sales = Sales − Returns inwards
- Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Returns outwards + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
- Gross profit = Net sales − Cost of goods sold
- Net profit = Gross profit + Other income − Expenses
- Working capital = Current assets − Current liabilities
! Carriage inwards: trading account. Carriage outwards: profit and loss.

title: Adjustment effects
lines: | Adjustment | Income statement | Balance sheet
| Outstanding expense | Add to expense | Current liability
| Prepaid expense | Deduct from expense | Current asset
| Accrued income | Add to income | Current asset
| Income in advance | Deduct from income | Current liability
| Depreciation | Expense | Deduct from asset
| Bad debts | Expense | Deduct from debtors
| Provision increase | Expense (increase only) | Deduct from debtors
| Closing stock | Credit trading | Current asset

title: Correcting a draft profit
lines: | Item found | Effect on profit
| Expense outstanding | −
| Expense prepaid | +
| Income accrued | +
| Income received in advance | −
| Depreciation or bad debt omitted | −
| Closing stock undervalued | +
| Capital item charged as expense | +

title: Capital or revenue?
lines: - Capital expenditure: buying or improving a fixed asset, plus carriage, installation and legal costs to bring it into use.
- Revenue expenditure: repairs, repainting, fuel, wages, rent, running insurance.
- Capital receipt: sale of a fixed asset, loan, new capital.
- Revenue receipt: sales, commission, interest, rent received.
! Capital treated as revenue: profit and assets both understated.

title: Depreciation methods
lines: | Method | Charge | Book value
| Straight-line | (Cost − Residual) ÷ Life, same yearly | Falls evenly, can reach residual or nil
| Reducing balance | Fixed % of book value, falls yearly | Never reaches nil
- Profit or loss on sale = Proceeds − (Cost − Accumulated depreciation)
- Land is normally not depreciated.

title: Bank reconciliation
lines: | From cash book (Dr) to bank statement | Action
| Cheques issued, not presented | Add
| Cheques deposited, not credited | Deduct
- First update the cash book for charges, interest, direct credits and dishonoured cheques.
- From the bank statement back to the cash book: reverse each sign.
! A positive balance is a debit in the cash book but a credit on the bank statement.

title: Partnership without a deed
lines: Partnership Act, 1932 rules when nothing is agreed:
| Item | Rule
| Profits and losses | Shared equally
| Interest on capital | None
| Interest on drawings | None
| Partner's salary | None
| Interest on partner's loan | 6 % a year
! Partners' liability is unlimited.

title: Bills of exchange
lines: - Drawer: creditor who writes the bill. Drawee: debtor who accepts it.
- Promissory note: a promise made by the debtor (maker).
- Due date = date + period + 3 days of grace.
- Discount on discounting = Amount × Rate × Months/12.
| Party | Entry on acceptance
| Drawer | Bills Receivable Dr, Debtor Cr
| Drawee | Creditor Dr, Bills Payable Cr
! On dishonour, charge the debtor the bill amount plus noting charges.
